rubrics.evidence: All three network-facing stages now receive subscription data as one cohesive value. ProxyImporter.readFromServer changed from 7 positional params (url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy, proxyProtocol) to `subscription: ProxyServerSubscription`. RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport changed from 6 positional params to `subscription: ProxyRulesSubscription`. SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText changed from 6 positional params to `config: SubscriptionConnectionConfig`. A new `SubscriptionConnectionConfig` interface (url, username, password, applyProxy) was added in definitions.ts, with `ProxyServerSubscription implements ... SubscriptionConnectionConfig` and `IExternalRulesConfig extends SubscriptionConnectionConfig`. All call sites in SubscriptionUpdater.ts and settingsPage.ts now pass the subscription object directly (e.g., `ProxyImporter.readFromServer(subscription, ...)` and `RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(subscription, ...)`) instead of unpacking individual fields.
rubrics.criterion: Every network-facing subscription read stage - the proxy-server subscription reader, the rules subscription reader, and the shared download transport they use - now receives the subscription request data (URL, credentials, payload obfuscation, expected format, apply-proxy mode, and where applicable the protocol override) as one cohesive value instead of declaring each of those settings as separate positional parameters.

rubrics.evidence: All seven production read sites now hand over the subscription object as a single cohesive value. In SubscriptionUpdater.ts, the scheduled refreshes call `ProxyImporter.readFromServer(subscription, ...)` and `RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(subscription, ...)` instead of unpacking fields. In settingsPage.ts, the server save (`ProxyImporter.readFromServer(subscriptionModel, ...)`), server test (`ProxyImporter.readFromServer(subscriptionModel, ...)`), rules save (`RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(editingSubscription, ...)`), rules test (`RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(subscriptionModel, ...)`), and rules-grid refresh (`RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(subscriptionModel, ...)`) all pass the model directly. The entry points and shared helper now take a single subscription/config object: `readFromServer(subscription: ProxyServerSubscription, ...)`, `readFromServerAndImport(subscription: ProxyRulesSubscription, ...)`, and `SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText(config: SubscriptionConnectionConfig, ...)`.
rubrics.criterion: All read flows that hold a stored subscription or an editor-bound subscription model - the scheduled background refresh for both subscription kinds, the settings-page save actions for both kinds, the two test actions, and the rules-grid refresh action - hand over one cohesive subscription/request value to the read entry points instead of forwarding individual connection fields as separate arguments.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch stops at the network boundary and does not refactor the batch importers. ProxyImporter.importText/parseText/parseJson retain the smell's loose parameters (e.g. importText(..., obfuscation?, format?, proxyProtocol?), parseText(text, obfuscation?, proxyProtocol?), parseJson(text, obfuscation?)), and RuleImporter.importRulesBatch still has loose (obfuscation: string, format: ExternalRulesFormat, ...) in its signature. readFromServerAndImport even forwards subscription.obfuscation and subscription.format as individual args to importRulesBatch, so those settings are not obtained from a cohesive request value inside the import stages.
rubrics.criterion: The batch import stages that consume the payload-describing subset (the proxy text/JSON list importer with its obfuscation, format and protocol inputs, and the rules batch importer with its obfuscation and format inputs) obtain those settings from the cohesive request value (or a value derived from it) rather than keeping them as stand-alone loose parameters in their signatures.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch reverts the exploded signatures: ProxyImporter.readFromServer now takes `subscription: ProxyServerSubscription`, RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport takes `subscription: ProxyRulesSubscription`, and SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText takes `config: SubscriptionConnectionConfig`. Callers in SubscriptionUpdater.ts and settingsPage.ts pass the subscription object directly (e.g., `ProxyImporter.readFromServer(subscription, ...)` and `RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(subscriptionModel, ...)`) instead of enumerating url/username/password/obfuscation/format/applyProxy positionally.
rubrics.criterion: No subscription read stage or importer still enumerates the connection/payload settings as a row of individual parameters (for example a signature still listing url, username, password, obfuscation, format, applyProxy positionally), and no caller still forwards those fields one-by-one into a read entry point.

rubrics.evidence: The rules import modal in settingsPage.ts reads `sourceType` from `#cmbImportRulesFormat` and calls `RuleImporter.importRulesBatch(null, sourceType, text, file, append, ...)`, supplying the UI-selected format through the batch-importer interface. The agent's patch does not touch this modal call site (its settingsPage.ts hunks only cover the subscription readFromServer/readFromServerAndImport calls at lines ~3711–4220), and it does not alter `importRulesBatch`'s `(obfuscation, format, ...)` signature, so the modal's format selection still drives AutoProxy/SwitchyOmega parsing, deduplication, and reporting unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: The rules file/text import modal in the settings page supplies the import request data it owns (at minimum the source format selected in the UI) through the refactored batch-importer interface, so importing a locally selected AutoProxy or SwitchyOmega file or pasted text still parses, deduplicates and reports exactly as before.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch leaves the local import path untouched: it changes ProxyImporter.readFromServer and SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText to accept a subscription/SubscriptionConnectionConfig, but does not modify ProxyImporter.importText. Per smell.diff, importText remains importText(text, file, append, currentProxies, success, fail?, obfuscation?, format?, proxyProtocol?) with no url/username/password/applyProxy connection fields required, and its parseText/parseJson success/fail handling is unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: The local proxy-list import modal still imports a selected file or pasted text without supplying any network-oriented request data, via an interface that does not require subscription connection fields where they do not apply, and with unchanged success/failure handling of the imported proxies.

rubrics.evidence: The patch bundles the reader/fetch signatures instead of leaving adapters: ProxyImporter.readFromServer now takes subscription: ProxyServerSubscription, RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport takes subscription: ProxyRulesSubscription, and SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText takes config: SubscriptionConnectionConfig. Call sites in SubscriptionUpdater.ts and settingsPage.ts pass subscription/subscriptionModel/editingSubscription directly, removing the previous subscription.url, subscription.username, ... positional forwarding. No shim, overload, or temporary field-by-field helper is introduced to re-explode the cohesive value before these calls.
rubrics.criterion: No leftover call adapter remains anywhere in the extension sources: no site still forwards exploded fields into a now-bundling signature via positional spread, temporary field-by-field helpers, or shim/overload forms that merely re-explode the cohesive value right before each call it replaced.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText now takes a single config: SubscriptionConnectionConfig whose interface declares only url, username, password, applyProxy — all four are read in the body (config.applyProxy for setSpecialUrl, config.url for fetch, config.username/config.password for the Basic-auth header). The previously inert obfuscation and format parameters are removed from the transport signature and from SubscriptionConnectionConfig; they remain only on the concrete subscription types and are consumed by the parse step (importRulesBatch, parseText, parseJson) where they are genuinely used.
rubrics.criterion: Every parameter of the refactored subscription read path is genuinely consumed by its receiving function; in particular the shared download transport no longer declares request fields that its own body never reads (the pair mirrored into it was inert), or it now actually performs the work those fields were mirrored for.

rubrics.evidence: The patch removes the now-unused `SpecialRequestApplyProxyMode` import from `ProxyImporter.ts` and `RuleImporter.ts` (where it was only needed to annotate the exploded positional params) and replaces it with the concrete subscription types; `SubscriptionFetch.ts` swaps its `SpecialRequestApplyProxyMode` import for `SubscriptionConnectionConfig`. No translator wrappers are introduced—call sites pass the subscription object directly—and the unused `obfuscation`/`format` parameters are dropped from `fetchSubscriptionText`.
rubrics.criterion: The rework leaves no dead residue of the exploded style behind: no now-unused imports, types, or fields kept only to satisfy the old positional forms, and no wrapper functions that exist only to translate between the new cohesive value and the old parameter row.

rubrics.evidence: In SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText, the agent patch preserves the credential logic unchanged: the `if (config.username)` guard means no Authorization header is sent when username is absent; when present, `let pass = atob(config.password)` decodes the password and `btoa(config.username + ':' + pass)` builds the identical Basic-auth header, all before `fetch(config.url, fetchRequest)` is issued. Only parameter access changed from individual params to `config.xxx`.
rubrics.criterion: Credential handling is unchanged on every read path: subscriptions without a username still send requests with no Authorization header, and subscriptions with a username still send the identical Basic-auth header (still built from the base64-decoded password, still before the request is issued, so decode failures surface synchronously).

rubrics.evidence: SubscriptionFetch.fetchSubscriptionText still gates registration with `if (config.applyProxy !== null) ProxyEngineSpecialRequests.setSpecialUrl(config.url, config.applyProxy);`. The readers now take the subscription object directly (`ProxyImporter.readFromServer(subscription, ...)` and `RuleImporter.readFromServerAndImport(subscription, ...)`) and forward it to SubscriptionFetch, so the helper observes the model's current applyProxy rather than a copied primitive. In settingsPage.ts the server and rules test call sites are changed only to pass `subscriptionModel`/`editingSubscription` directly; the surrounding pre-register/clear flow is not modified by the patch, leaving those test actions unchanged.
rubrics.criterion: Special-request registration is preserved: a subscription URL is still registered only when its apply-proxy mode differs from null, and the settings-page test flows still pre-register the request, clear the mode on the bound model, and have the reader observe the cleared value - unchanged on server and rules test actions.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only swaps unpacked positional fields for the subscription/config object; response and document handling are unchanged. SubscriptionFetch still calls success(responseText, response.status, response.statusText) and fail on network error. ProxyImporter still parses only when statusCode === 200 and otherwise calls fail(new Error(`${statusCode}, ${statusText}`)), and for 200 still calls ajaxSuccess(responseText) so an empty body continues into doImport/parseText. RuleImporter still routes the body through ajaxSuccess(responseText) into importRulesBatch with subscription.obfuscation/format; the empty-body guard and batch import path are not modified.
rubrics.criterion: Response and document handling is unchanged: only HTTP 200 bodies are parsed, other statuses still fail with an error carrying the status code and status text, empty or blank documents still fail rather than import, the rules reader still never produces an empty rule container from a blank body, and the proxy-server reader's historical continue-into-import path for an empty body is intact.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch only changes parameter threading (passing subscription objects instead of unpacked fields) and does not alter any parsing logic. In ProxyImporter.ts, parseText still checks `if (obfuscation)` and decodes base64 via `atob`, still sets `defaultProxyProtocol = "HTTP"` with override `if (proxyProtocol)`, and parseJson still decodes base64 the same way; doImport still branches on `format != null && format == ProxyServerSubscriptionFormat.Json` to select parseJson vs parseText. In RuleImporter.ts, doImport still checks `obfuscation?.toLowerCase() == 'base64'` for decoding, still dispatches `if (formatParam == ExternalRulesFormat.AutoProxy)` (detect then parse) and `else if (formatParam == ExternalRulesFormat.SwitchyOmega)` (parseAndCompile), with no else clause for other formats. The importRulesBatch and importText signatures are unchanged from the smell state, and the agent correctly threads subscription.obfuscation/format/proxyProtocol into them.
rubrics.criterion: Parsing behavior is unchanged for every format: base64-obfuscated payloads are still decoded before parsing in plain-text lists, JSON lists, and rule batches; JSON-format server subscriptions still take the JSON branch; text lines still default their protocol to HTTP unless a protocol override is given; rule batches still dispatch AutoProxy (detect then parse) versus SwitchyOmega (parse, compile, convert) and still fail for any other format value.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only swaps unpacked positional arguments back to passing the subscription object; callback bodies and stats/persistence steps are left intact. In SubscriptionUpdater.ts the `subscription.stats = new SubscriptionStats()` reset before each read and the `{success, message, result}`/`{success, message, rules}` callback type annotations are unchanged. SubscriptionFetch still performs the same side effects (setSpecialUrl when applyProxy!==null, Basic auth header when username set, fetch GET no-store) and invokes success with (responseText, status, statusText) and fail with error, so no read path lost or reordered observable behavior.
rubrics.criterion: No read path lost or reordered its observable side effects: every scheduled refresh still updates the subscription's stats on success and failure and still persists the fetched proxies/rules together with the existing change notifications, and no success/failure callback payload changed shape ({success, message, result: ProxyServer[]} for proxy lists and {success, message, rules: {whiteList, blackList}} for imported rules).
